title: ACEF Harm Core Taxonomy (closed harm_class / realization / causality enums + core->scheme derivation rows)
description: The ACEF-owned harm_core vocabulary for RFC-0002 (ACEF core_version 1.1.0; §5.2, Appendix E Q14). Carries the closed enums the incident_card harm_core $ref's (`harm_class`, `realization`, `causality`, `tangibility`) AND the concrete one-directional core->scheme derivation rows (`harm_class` -> {nist_ai_600_1, cset, mit_domain, oecd}) against which a present taxonomy_crosswalk member is checked (ACEF-085). The harm_class code list is NORMATIVE in RFC §5.2 (enumerated here, keyed to EU Art. 3(49)(a-d) plus the AI-specific intangible classes); the derivation-table STRUCTURE is normative in §5.2 and the concrete ACEF-side ROWS are materialized here. Because this taxonomy is ACEF-owned (not transcribed from an external source) the rows can be authored directly; where a row depends on an EXTERNAL scheme value-set not yet transcribed (OECD criterion #3/#19 closed sets, NIST-final drift, MIT subdomains, CSET axes), that target is left on the v1.2 closed-enum surface (§5.5 / §10) and the row carries only the ACEF-side projection plus an explicit `external_value_set_status` of `transcribed` or `v1_2_closed_enum_surface`. Derivation is one-directional and MAY be a partial map: an UNMAPPABLE core value leaves the corresponding crosswalk member absent (not an error); only a PRESENT crosswalk member that CONTRADICTS the core is an error (ACEF-085). This file is a closed-enum data artifact, NOT a payload schema; it is referenced by incident_card.schema.json#/properties/harm_core and (for the eu_ai_act trigger keying) by taxonomy_crosswalk.schema.json. Deterministic: all arrays are sorted ascending by RFC-8785 canonical byte order of their elements (§5.10); no wall-clock or random values.

harm_class.description: Closed ACEF-owned harm taxonomy keyed to EU Art. 3(49)(a-d) plus the AI-specific intangible classes (RFC §5.2; the code list is normative). These are ACEF class NAMES, NOT the EU Art. 3(49) `3.49.*` TRIGGER codes (those live under taxonomy_crosswalk.eu_ai_act.serious_incident_triggers[]). The tangible/intangible split is a separate derived `tangibility` field (§5.2).

realization.description: Whether the harm materialized, is an issue, or was a near miss (CSET imminency / AIID harm-or-near-harm; RFC §5.2). Closed enum.

causality.description: Normalized attribution across the supply chain (MIT Causal Taxonomy; RFC §5.2). Closed object: entity x intent x timing.

tangibility.description: Tangible vs intangible harm (RFC §5.2). Derived field carried alongside harm_class; one of the EU Art. 3(49) keys.

art3_49_trigger_keying.description: One-directional keying of the four EU Art. 3(49)(a-d) trigger letters to their ACEF harm_class names (RFC §5.2). The `3.49.*` codes are EU AI Act CROSSWALK trigger values (taxonomy_crosswalk.eu_ai_act.serious_incident_triggers[]), NOT harm_class names. This table lets a validator check that a present eu_ai_act trigger is consistent with the card's harm_class (ACEF-085) without conflating the two namespaces. Note that `3.49.a` (physical_health) covers BOTH death AND non-fatal serious health harm; the 10-day clock keys on the separate `death_involved` fact, not on the trigger (§5.7).

rows.note: Death OR serious harm to a person's health (death takes the 10-day clock via death_involved; non-fatal health harm takes the general 15-day clock, §5.7).
Serious and irreversible disruption of the management or operation of critical infrastructure (2-day clock, §5.7).
Infringement of obligations under Union law intended to protect fundamental rights; the `widespread` modifier of this trigger drives the 2-day clock (§5.7).
Serious harm to property or the environment.

derivation_rows.description: Concrete ACEF-side one-directional core->scheme derivation rows (RFC §5.2; ACEF-085 dependency). For each harm_class, the projection into the closed crosswalk scheme members the row is responsible for: `nist_ai_600_1` (closed category-name set, edition 2024-07-final, verified in §5.5), `cset` (csetv1 harm_type axis), `mit_domain` (MIT AI Risk Repository domain), `oecd` (OECD common reporting framework harm-type criterion #11 ordinal hint). A present crosswalk member that contradicts the row's projection for the card's harm_class is an ACEF-085 error; an UNMAPPABLE projection (empty `members`) leaves the member legitimately absent (not an error). `external_value_set_status` records whether the target scheme's CLOSED value enumeration is already transcribed from its primary source (`transcribed`) or remains on the v1.2 closed-enum conformance surface (`v1_2_closed_enum_surface`, §5.5 / §10) — in the latter case the ACEF-side projection is authoritative for derivation but the target enum is not yet closed in v1.1. All member arrays are sorted ascending by RFC-8785 canonical byte order (§5.10).
